entities.summary:
Giovanni Conti (1414–1493) was an Italian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a significant role in the Catholic Church during the Renaissance period.

As a prominent figure in the papal hierarchy, Conti was instrumental in shaping church doctrine and policy. His tenure as a cardinal saw him participate in several high-stakes conclaves, including those that elected Pope Innocent VIII and Pope Alexander VI.

Conti's influence extended beyond the Vatican, as he was also involved in various diplomatic efforts between the Catholic Church and European monarchies. He collaborated with prominent figures such as Lorenzo de' Medici, the ruler of Florence, to promote Catholic interests in Italy.

Despite his significant contributions to the Catholic Church, Conti's legacy has been subject to varying interpretations among historians. Some view him as a conservative who opposed the growing influence of humanism, while others see him as a pragmatist who navigated complex alliances to advance Catholic interests.

One lasting impact of Conti's career was his involvement in the Council of Basel, where he played a key role in shaping the church's response to the Protestant Reformation. His efforts helped to maintain Catholic unity and paved the way for future ecumenical councils.
